helpers.name: tower_mod_div_byte__byte_encoding
helpers.strategy: Prove forall z d q : Z, 0 < d -> 0 < q -> ((z mod (d * 256 * q)) / d) mod 256 = (z / d) mod 256. Use the Euclidean quotient/remainder decomposition for z by d*256*q and the positive-divisor addition/multiplication laws; division changes by a multiple of 256*q, removed by the final modulo. This holds for negative z as well. Used by the machine-byte bridge with d=256^k and q=256^(7-k).

helpers.name: tower_machine_byte__byte_encoding
helpers.strategy: Prove forall z k : Z, 0 <= k <= 7 -> unsigned_last_nbits ((Z.quot (unsigned_last_nbits z 64) (256^k)) mod 256) 8 = tower_encode_byte z k. Unfold unsigned truncation to modulo powers of two; remove outer 8-bit truncation by modulo idempotence, use nonnegativity of z mod 2^64 to replace quot by div, apply tower_mod_div_byte__byte_encoding with d=256^k and q=256^(7-k), then enumerate k=0..7 and combine iterated positive floor divisions to division by 256^k. All positivity and power identities are numeric after the finite case split. No signed-range premise is needed, which is essential for entail_wit_1 splits.
